questions.q: A test method inserts a record and calls a service method, but never checks the result with an assertion. What does a passing result for this test actually prove?
options: That the code is fully correct
That the code met 100% coverage
Only that no unhandled exception was thrown — nothing about whether the result was actually correct
That the record was rolled back successfully
questions.explain: Without a real assertion tied to the expected outcome, a passing test only proves the code didn't blow up — it says nothing about whether the behavior is actually correct.

questions.q: In System.assertEquals(expected, actual), what is the correct argument order?
options: The actual value first, then the expected value
The expected value first, then the actual value
Order doesn't matter for this method
Both arguments must be identical types or it won't compile
questions.explain: System.assertEquals takes the expected value first and the actual value second — getting this backwards doesn't break the test but makes failure messages confusing to read.

questions.q: Which class does Salesforce's current Apex Reference Guide document as the modern, recommended way to write test assertions?
options: The Test class
The Limits class
The Assert class
The Database class
questions.explain: The Assert class (Assert.areEqual, Assert.isTrue, Assert.isNull, etc.) is the current recommended style, though the older System.assert* methods still compile and run.

questions.q: What is Assert.fail() typically used for?
options: To intentionally crash the Salesforce org for debugging
To force a test failure inside a try/catch block when an expected exception did not actually occur
To skip a test method without running it
To automatically retry a failed assertion
questions.explain: Assert.fail() is commonly used inside a try/catch in a test that expects an exception, to force a failure if the code under test didn't actually throw when it should have.

questions.q: What happens immediately when an assertion fails during a test method?
options: The method pauses and waits for manual input
Execution of that test method halts with a fatal error, and any assertions after it never run
The failure is silently logged and the test continues to completion
The entire test class is automatically deleted
questions.explain: A failed assertion halts execution of that test method immediately with a fatal error that can't be caught in a try/catch, so nothing after the failed line executes.
